source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 4 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Ilarion»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιλάριος ο Θαυματουργός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and the rank matches: doxologia's «Sfântul Cuvios Ilarion» against saint.gr's Όσιος. **There is exactly one candidate of that name on this Greek day**, which is why this is drafted as an upgrade at all; the folder is bare on the Romanian side and the Greek is the first source to say anything about him. **But the name form is not the same word**: saint.gr prints Ιλάριος, Hilarius, and the Romanian form the folder holds is Ilarion, which answers to Ιλαρίων. Both are recorded — the Greek form as the page prints it — and **nothing is transliterated across**; if a later reader decides Ιλάριος and Ilarion are two men, this row is the one to undo, and no folder was created that would have to be merged. **The Greek adds what he was and what he did**: a worthy worker of the Gospel early, given the grace of wonders, healing paralytics and the lame, breaking a drought by his prayer and freeing many possessed in the name of Jesus Christ; a withdrawal to a desert place and a hut, where he studied and prayed; a return to society and, at the common demand, ordination as a priest, in which he discharged all the duties of a good presbyter. **It prints no year and no place**, so `dates` stays absent, and the epithet ο Θαυματουργός is not put in `types` as `wonderworker` because the folder's existing `types` is the Romanian reading and adding to it is a separate claim; the page's word is quoted in the life instead. Its couplet works on the name: «Ἔγνων τὸν Ἱλάριον ἱλαρὸν φύσει, / Ὃς θαυματουργεῖ ἐν τάφῳ τεθειμένος» — I knew Hilarius to be cheerful by nature, who works wonders laid in his grave. No hymn, no relic.
